name: doomformer
cost: Free (MIT). Some bundled data has its own licence
works_with: Python 3.11+ on Linux or macOS. The museum map also runs in GZDoom, LZDoom, UZDoom and ZDoom 2.8.1
short: Compiles small integer neural networks into DOOM maps, where voodoo dolls do the maths and every value is checked against NumPy.
what: doomformer turns a neural network into a DOOM map. A value is a crowd of voodoo dolls, a weight is a line on the floor that adds to the sum each time a doll crosses it, and a sum is a light level or floor height. Python reads the values back and checks every one against NumPy with zero tolerance. The demos include an MNIST digit reader, a small transformer that names a level and a museum map you can play.
who: People who like neural networks, compilers or DOOM mapping and enjoy an odd experiment. A small network runs about 23,000 times slower than NumPy, so this is for curiosity and learning.
needs: Python 3.11 or newer, on Linux or macOS
git, cmake and a C compiler, so `doomformer doctor` can build the ACS compiler if it's missing
For the museum map without Python: GZDoom and the free Freedoom IWAD

steps.title: Install it
steps.code: pip install git+https://github.com/mottopanikeiku/doomformer   # Python 3.11+, Linux or macOS

steps.title: Check your setup
steps.text: It builds ACC, the ACS compiler, if it's missing. On Fedora: `sudo dnf install git cmake gcc gcc-c++ make`.

steps.title: Run the first demos
steps.text: The first checks a small network in about 2 seconds. The second has the marine walk a 7 and the level read it.
steps.code:
doomformer hello             # 2 s: a small MLP, every value checked
doomformer draw --digit 7    # 15 s: the marine walks a 7 and the level reads it

steps.title: Play the museum
steps.text: Download museum.wad from the v0.7.1 release and the Freedoom IWAD. Step on pads to light a digit, press READ, then press MUTATE to rewire one connection.

steps.title: Or skip the install
steps.text: Open the Colab notebook linked in the README and draw a digit in your browser.

try.label: From the README
try.text: `doomformer draw --digit 7`. The marine inks a 7 on the floor, presses READ, and 1,355 voodoo dolls in the map work out which digit it is.

watch: Bigger runs are slow. `doomformer ask` takes about 11 minutes, and all 10,000 MNIST digits take about 23 minutes on six games. Budget one core and 1.3 GB of RAM per game.
EXACT means DOOM got the same numbers as the integer network. It doesn't mean the answer is right, and inputs that never ran aren't covered.
Some showcased outputs and seeds were hand-picked.
The fruit-fly circuits in `models/fly` are CC BY-NC 4.0, so non-commercial use only.
The museum.wad download has a SHA-256 file you can check it against.
